finding_id.description: The id the requester assigned to the new finding.

observation.description: What was seen, in the noticer's own words.

where.description: Where it was seen: a file and line, a page address, a run id or a step in a process.

noticed_by.description: Who noticed it: a person, a worker or an automated check.

noticed_at.description: When it was noticed, as a UTC date and time.

required: Record it now, even if it looks small or will be fixed in a minute; recording never waits for a fix.
Write what was seen, where, who noticed it and when. For an annoyance, quote the person's words exactly.

Choose a provisional kind and severity from the guides and compute the fingerprint by the kind definitions' rule. Compare it with any pinned nearby findings and note a match instead of skipping the record.

Remove credentials, personal data and private paths; say where a secret is, never its value. Set sensitivity to security, and public to false, when the problem could expose data, grant access or spend beyond a grant.
Set status open. Never delete or rewrite an earlier finding; a correction is a later version or a new finding.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.
